title: Soft-launch adaptive weight drift caused capacity surge and pinned shardset unpin failure
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Summary: During a soft-launch (progressive weight ramp) of model variant model-7b-v2 on region-us-east, we observed an unexpected drift in assigned routing weights that rapidly escalated traffic to the new variant from the intended ~5% to ~60% over a 7-minute window. The sudden traffic concentration caused GPU pool saturation and increased tail latency and error rates. An automated rollback was attempted but failed due to a pinned shardset lock left by a coincident maintenance task, preventing orchestrator unpin operations. Manual mitigation required emergency traffic reroute and transient capacity increases. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-01T09:02Z - Soft-launch started: weight ramp plan scheduled (2% -> 5% over 10 min)
2026-03-01T09:05Z - Monitoring alerted: 95th token latency for model-7b-v2 exceeded 600ms (threshold 300ms)
2026-03-01T09:08Z - Traffic weight at controller reported 62% for model-7b-v2 despite planned 5%
2026-03-01T09:09Z - Autoscaler triggered but saw pinned shardset lock and could not preemptively scale up new shard allocation
2026-03-01T09:12Z - Automated rollback initiated by rollout controller; rollback request returned 409 (pin lock) and timed out
2026-03-01T09:16Z - On-call manually opened emergency routing rule to force 100% fallback to model-7b-v1 using edge header override
2026-03-01T09:25Z - GPU utilization on shardset peaked at 98%; error rates normalized after manual reroute
2026-03-01T10:00Z - Maintenance job identified: shard pin task from scheduled backup (coordination bug) - released pin with operator intervention
2026-03-02 - Incident review kickoff with Eng, Prod, and Platform; initial RCA drafted
root_cause_summary: Three contributing defects combined: 1) a header canonicalization difference between CDN edge and regional proxy caused the rollout controller to mis-evaluate routing fingerprints, producing stale entropy leading the adaptive weight controller to apply aggressive weight decay/math in the wrong routing bucket; 2) a regression in the weight-decay algorithm allowed multiplicative growth under low-sample conditions, amplifying the drift; 3) an unrelated maintenance task left a shardset version pin that blocked orchestrator rollback/unpin operations during the surge.
impact: Customer-facing latency and error rate spike for users routed through us-east for ~14 minutes. Several high-throughput customers saw degraded throughput; internal SLIs for P95 latencies and error-rates breached. No persistent data loss. Estimated affected requests: ~1.4M tokens served with elevated tail latency.
comments: 2026-03-01 10:30 - Marco Liu: Initial mitigation succeeded. We routed traffic to fallback and reduced error rates. Need to harden rollout controller to detect header ambiguity.
2026-03-02 14:00 - Priya Nair (SRE): Confirmed scheduled backup left pin. Adding guard in scheduler to avoid pins during active rollouts.
2026-03-03 09:15 - Dan Park (Runtime): Reproduced weight drift locally when header hash namespaces are inconsistent; creating unit tests for header normalization and rollout simulation.

2026-03-04 16:40 - Aisha Banerjee (PM): Prioritizing emergency fixes: header normalization, weight-decay patch, and an emergency unpin API for operator use. Drafting rollout policy changes for soft-launch velocity limits.
2026-03-08 11:20 - Design review note: Console should show per-route canonical header mapping during rollout preview. Adding to console roadmap as low-effort improvement.
action_items: AI-1: Implement header canonicalization layer in rollout controller that normalizes edge/CDN header casing and maps legacy header aliases (owner: Dan Park, estimate: 3) - GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12411

AI-2: Patch weight-decay algorithm to clamp multiplicative increases under low-sample regimes and add deterministic seed for offline simulation (owner: Runtime team, estimate: 5) - GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8802

AI-3: Add an emergency-unpin operator API with audit and two-step confirmation; only available to SRE and Platform on-call (owner: Platform, estimate: 3) - design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/rollout-unpin
AI-4: Scheduler change to prevent scheduled maintenance pins during active rollouts and add cross-check: deny pin if rollout window open (owner: SRE, estimate: 2) - ticket: ENG-87250
AI-5: Create integration test in CI that runs a simulated progressive ramp with header-stripping proxy to validate stable weights under proxy transformations (owner: QA, estimate: 4)

AI-6: Add runbook step: if rollback fails due to pin, execute 'emergency-unpin' followed by controlled reroute; include runbook in on-call playbooks (owner: SRE, estimate: 1) - runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/oncall-docs/pull/77

AI-7: Dashboard and alerting: add 'weighted-variance' metric for rollout controller and alert if weight deviation > 15% from plan within 5 min (owner: Observability, estimate: 2) - dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/rollouts
AI-8: Postmortem writeup in Confluence with customer impact timeline and L1 talking points for support (owner: Aisha Banerjee, estimate: 1) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/model-rollout-87234
acceptance_criteria: Header canonicalization PR merged and deployed to staging; integration test passes for proxy-stripping scenario
Weight-decay patch merged and validated with synthetic workload showing no multiplicative amplification under low-sample conditions
Emergency-unpin API implemented with RBAC and audit logs and exercised in a dry-run during the next oncall drill
Scheduler change deployed so maintenance pins cannot be applied while rollout windows are active
Dashboards and alerting for weighted-variance are live and new alert fires in simulated test
